licences.notes: Words as printed in the Peters vocal score: fà, Guglielmo's “di riso di, riso” (the comma as printed), “si troverà” (not in the libretto), and Don Alfonso's “belba” for bella in bar 61, a print slip.

licences.source: Edition Peters vocal score (Edition Peters Nr. 4474, plate 11446, edited by Georg Schünemann), pages 358–366, bars 576–671 of No. 31
licences.author: Kurt Soldan (1891–1946), piano reduction
licences.notes: Written out from the printed pages: the No. 31 Finale (671 bars) read in fourteen page ranges, sung lines and piano each by two independent readers, every disagreement settled on the zoomed page by a judge, a separate sweep for dynamics and other marks, then checked bar by bar by eight fresh proofreaders (pages 360–366 clean). The German singing translation is left out. All the singers of this section have a staff throughout, with rests where the print leaves a staff out; singers who do not sing in this section are left out. Cut from the one-file finale at bars 576–671: from the Allegro molto, after the bar of rest with a fermata, to the end of the opera (“Ende der Oper”); the voices enter at bar 9, and bars 89–96 are for the piano alone. A slur printed in bar 36 between the two voices of the right hand is not encoded; the bracketed circle-cross in bar 88 is a remark only. Playback tempo ♩ = 222 (a half note = 111) from René Jacobs's recording (harmonia mundi), 1:44.
